a_records.quote: Theorem 3.8. Suppose X1, . . . , Xn and X∗1, . . . , X∗n are independent samples with Xi ~ ENH(α1, λ1, βi), and Xi∗ ~ ENH(α2, λ2, βi∗), i = 1, . . . , n. Then for α1 ≤ α2 and λ > 0, we have Σi=1^n βi = Σi=1^n βi∗ ⟹ Xn:n ≥c X∗n:n.
a_records.family: ENH(α1, λ1, βi) vs ENH(α2, λ2, βi∗)
a_records.compared: equal sums of β's, outer shapes α1 ≤ α2

hypotheses.formal: outer shape ordering (λ1, λ2 arbitrary per setup)

a_records.ambiguity: Statement says 'α1 ≤ α2 and λ > 0' — presumably means λ1, λ2 > 0 since λ1, λ2 both appear; the convexity of h(x) = ((1+λ2x)^{α2/α1} − 1)/λ1 only needs α2 ≥ α1.

b_records.quote: Suppose X1, ..., Xn and X1*, ..., Xn* are independent samples with Xi ~ ENH(alpha1, lambda1, betai), and Xi* ~ ENH(alpha2, lambda2, betai*), i = 1, ..., n. Then for alpha1 <= alpha2 and lambda > 0, we have sum_{i=1}^n betai = sum_{i=1}^n betai* ==> Xn:n >=c Xn:n*.
b_records.family: ENH(alpha1, lambda1, betai) vs ENH(alpha2, lambda2, betai*)
b_records.compared: Xn:n vs Xn:n* in convex transform order

hypotheses.text: alpha1 <= alpha2 and lambda > 0 (printed; lambda1, lambda2 appear in the proof's quantile-composition h(x) = ((1+lambda2 x)^{alpha2/alpha1} - 1)/lambda1)

b_records.ambiguity: '>=c' is the convex transform order (Definition 2.x of the paper). The printed condition says 'lambda > 0' while the proof uses separate lambda1, lambda2 > 0.
